app.name: ProFolio
app.tagline: Turn a CV into a portfolio you control
app.footerNote: Your CV stays private. Only what you review and publish becomes public.

marketing.title: Your CV, published as a portfolio you actually control.
marketing.lead: Upload a PDF. Review every extracted fact. Compose your pages. Claim a URL and publish.
marketing.supporting: Nothing goes public until you say so, and no AI runs when a visitor loads your page.
marketing.howLead: Four steps, and you stay the editor of every one of them.

steps.uploadBody: A PDF, stored privately. Text is extracted locally before any model sees it.
steps.reviewBody: Every field is editable. Warnings point at the values worth a second look.
steps.composeBody: Reorder, hide, add sections and extra pages. No code, no templates to fight.
steps.publishBody: Pick your slug, preview the result, and publish when it reads right.

principles.controlBody: Extraction produces a draft. Publishing is always an explicit action you take.
principles.privacyBody: The uploaded file is never publicly addressable and you can delete it at any time.
principles.honestBody: The extractor is instructed to leave a field empty rather than guess at it.
principles.fastTitle: Public pages are cheap and fast
principles.fastBody: A published portfolio is served from a snapshot and needs no AI to render.

directory.title: The details worth checking before you upload a CV
directory.lead: Read about the workflow, factual-accuracy boundary, security model, accessible template, privacy choices, and practical support before creating an account.

useCases.title: A portfolio can lead with the evidence that fits the career
useCases.lead: The template stays consistent while the reviewed document decides which sections appear and what comes first.
useCases.engineerBody: Lead with systems, roles, project constraints, technologies, publications, and the outcomes already supported by your CV.
useCases.designerBody: Combine project narratives with owned gallery images, useful alternative text, courses, awards, and selected social profiles.
useCases.graduateBody: Bring education, projects, courses, languages, volunteering, and demonstrated skills forward when work history is still short.
useCases.consultantBody: Maintain separate portfolios for different audiences from one account without mixing their drafts or published addresses.

trust.title: The public page is separated from the machinery that created it
trust.lead: These are product behaviors, not performance claims: they describe what is stored, when it becomes public, and what a visitor request depends on.
trust.draftBody: Extraction can organize source facts, but only the owner can correct, compose, and publish them.
trust.snapshotBody: A visitor reads stored reviewed content; their request does not call the AI provider or parse the original PDF.
trust.ownershipBody: Dashboard operations resolve the signed-in owner before reading or changing a portfolio.
trust.accessTitle: Absent and private content stays absent
trust.accessBody: Hidden channels, empty sections, drafts, and unauthorized private pages are omitted from public output and navigation.

faq.title: What happens at the moments that matter
faq.lead: Short answers to the questions behind uploading, reviewing, publishing, and keeping a portfolio available.
faq.publishQuestion: Does uploading my CV publish anything?
faq.publishAnswer: No. Import creates a private draft. Publishing is a separate action after you have reviewed the content and public address.
faq.missingQuestion: What happens when the CV does not contain a field?
faq.missingAnswer: The field remains empty. The extractor is not allowed to complete a professional claim from plausibility alone.
faq.cvQuestion: Can visitors download my original CV?
faq.cvAnswer: The source upload remains private. A visitor can only access an attachment you explicitly add to a reviewed published document.
faq.outageQuestion: Does a published page need AI to load?
faq.outageAnswer: No. Published portfolios render from validated stored snapshots, independent of AI extraction and PDF parsing services.
faq.manyQuestion: Can one account publish more than one portfolio?
faq.manyAnswer: Yes. Each portfolio has its own draft, pages, theme choices, publication state, and public address.

cta.title: Start with a draft you can inspect
cta.description: Create a portfolio, import a readable PDF or begin manually, and decide what deserves to become public.

features.title: Everything needed to publish your professional story
features.description: Import facts, edit every field, compose pages, and publish one or many portfolios from one account.

sections.first: Reviewable CV extraction keeps every claim under your control.
sections.second: Flexible pages combine experience, projects, skills, education, and your own sections.
sections.third: Published snapshots stay fast even when authoring services are unavailable.
sections.thirdTitle: Snapshots that don't depend on us
sections.fourth: Reorder, hide, or remove any section — nothing is fixed, so the page matches the career, not a template.
sections.fifth: Publish a portfolio per role or audience from a single account, each with its own address and its own review.
sections.sixth: A downloadable PDF, an installable app, and a public feed come from the same published data — no separate setup.

how-it-works.title: From PDF to public portfolio in four deliberate steps
how-it-works.description: Upload, review, compose, then publish. Each boundary is visible and reversible.

sections.first: Your PDF is validated and read as a private source document.
sections.second: Extracted facts become an editable draft with warnings, never a public page.
sections.third: You choose the address and publish only after the preview is accurate.
sections.fourth: Import produces a draft, not a page — the address you choose stays unclaimed until you publish it yourself.
sections.fifth: Reopen the editor after publishing to update a role, add a project, or hide a page — changes stay private until you save and republish.
sections.sixth: The golden path from CV to public address takes minutes, not a template to fight with.

examples.title: Portfolios shaped by the work, not a demo template
examples.description: See how different careers remain recognisable inside one consistent, accessible system.

sections.first: Engineering portfolios foreground systems, outcomes, and technical depth.
sections.second: Design portfolios can pair project narratives with owned gallery media.
sections.third: Early-career portfolios can lead with education, courses, and demonstrable projects.
sections.fourth: A consultant or freelancer can publish a focused portfolio per specialty, each drawing from the same reviewed facts.
sections.fifth: Every portfolio shares the same accessible structure, so no two look alike, and none look unfinished.
sections.sixth: Import shows what your own CV produces before you decide whether to publish it.

templates.title: One disciplined template with room for an individual voice
templates.description: A stable information architecture keeps attention on evidence while themes adjust its tone.

sections.first: Semantic sections create a readable hierarchy on every screen size.
sections.second: Named accent and theme choices preserve tested contrast.
sections.third: No arbitrary scripts, styles, or embeds can compromise a visitor.
sections.fourth: Every theme ships in a light and dark variant that meets the same contrast bar, so a visitor's preference is never a downgrade.
sections.fifth: The template adapts to whichever sections are visible — a portfolio with only projects and skills looks intentional, not incomplete.
sections.sixth: Example portfolios show the same template carrying very different careers.

cv-import.title: CV import that treats the document as evidence
cv-import.description: The importer reports what it can support and leaves unsupported fields empty.

sections.first: PDF signatures and limits are checked before parsing begins.
sections.second: Extracted values retain warnings where a human review matters.
sections.third: The original CV remains private and importing never publishes.
sections.fourth: DOCX imports go through the same scanner-validated pipeline as a PDF before extraction begins.
sections.fifth: A field the CV doesn't contain stays empty rather than being filled with a plausible guess.
sections.sixth: Files that fail validation — the wrong type, too large, or unreadable — are refused with a reason, not silently accepted.

ai-accuracy.title: AI assists the draft; it never gets the final word
ai-accuracy.description: Structured extraction is constrained by a simple rule: missing evidence means an empty field.

sections.first: The model receives extracted text through a bounded structured contract.
sections.second: Schema validation rejects malformed output before it reaches the editor.
sections.third: Writing enhancements are separate actions and cannot silently replace facts.
sections.fourth: A deterministic fallback reads structured resume text directly when a model provider is unavailable, so import never depends on a single service staying up.
sections.fifthTitle: An instruction in a CV is still just text
sections.fifth: Content extracted from a document is treated as data to display, never as an instruction the assistant follows.
sections.sixth: Every extracted field appears in the editor for correction before anything reaches a published page.

security.title: Security boundaries designed around a private CV
security.description: Ownership checks, validated uploads, and isolated public snapshots reduce what any request can expose.

sections.first: Dashboard reads and writes are scoped to the authenticated owner.
sections.second: Uploads are identified by content, scanned, and stored under server-generated keys.
sections.third: Public rendering imports no authoring, parser, AI, or private-storage path.
sections.fourth: Any page can be given its own share password, checked server-side, without exposing which pages exist to someone who doesn't have it.
sections.fifthTitle: Guessing a draft address fails the same way
sections.fifth: An unpublished portfolio and a typo return the identical response, so probing addresses can't tell the two apart.
sections.sixth: A security concern reaches the team directly through the contact page — no need to describe it publicly first.

privacy.title: Your source document stays private by default
privacy.description: Only reviewed snapshot fields and explicitly public assets can reach a published address.

sections.first: A raw CV is never served from a public object URL.
sections.second: Hidden contact channels and pages are omitted rather than disguised.
sections.third: Account deletion removes identifying rows and owned files.
sections.firstTitle: No public link to a raw file
sections.fourth: A portfolio can opt out of search indexing entirely, or keep a specific page out of the sitemap while the rest stays public.
sections.fifth: A private page's grant is scoped to that exact page and locale — it doesn't unlock anything else.
sections.sixth: What the service does with what you upload is written out in the terms, not buried in a policy nobody reads.

about.title: A portfolio product built around factual authorship
about.description: ProFolio exists to shorten setup without taking authorship away from the person represented.

sections.first: The product begins with evidence already written in a CV.
sections.second: Editing and publishing remain explicit human decisions.
sections.third: Public pages are durable reads, not live AI demonstrations.
sections.fourth: Turning a CV into a presentable site used to mean a template fight or a freelancer's invoice — this collapses that into an import and a review.
sections.fifth: The product does one thing — CV to reviewed portfolio — rather than expanding into a general site builder.
sections.sixth: The mission page sets out the specific commitments this product is trying to keep.

mission.title: Make professional publishing honest and ownable
mission.description: A useful portfolio should be accessible to create, straightforward to verify, and dependable to visit.

sections.first: Reduce the mechanical cost of turning a CV into a coherent site.
sections.second: Never trade speed for plausible but unsupported professional claims.
sections.third: Give each person a stable address and control over what it says.
sections.fourthTitle: Accessible by default, not by request
sections.fourth: Every portfolio meets the same accessibility bar automatically — it isn't a setting someone has to know to turn on.
sections.fifth: A visitor can trust that what they're reading was reviewed by the person it describes, not generated for them a moment before.
sections.sixth: The features and security pages show what these commitments look like as working product decisions.

contact.title: Talk to the ProFolio team
contact.description: Ask about the product, report an accessibility problem, or share a security concern.

sections.first: Product questions receive practical answers about import, editing, and publishing.
sections.second: Accessibility reports should include the page, browser, and assistive technology used.
sections.third: Security reports are handled discreetly and never require sending your CV.
sections.fourth: The FAQ and help pages answer the most common questions about import, privacy, and publishing before you need to wait on a reply.
sections.fifthTitle: What we don't need from you
sections.fifth: A report never requires attaching your CV or sharing your account password — describe the problem, not the private document.
sections.sixth: Messages go to a small team directly, not a queue — expect a reply, not an autoresponder.

help.title: Help for each step from import to publish
help.description: Find direct guidance for common decisions and recoverable problems.

sections.first: Import help covers readable PDFs, limits, scans, and rejected files.
sections.second: Editor help explains visibility, ordering, previews, and warnings.
sections.third: Publishing help covers addresses, updates, private pages, and unpublishing.
sections.fourth: The FAQ page collects the questions people ask most before they ever open a support message.
sections.fifth: The changelog page explains recent changes that might affect what you're seeing in the editor or on a published page.
sections.sixth: The contact page reaches the team directly for anything this page doesn't answer.

faq.title: Questions people ask before trusting a CV importer
faq.description: Clear answers about AI, privacy, cost, ownership, and what happens after publishing.

sections.first: Nothing publishes automatically: every import produces a draft.
sections.second: Missing CV facts stay empty rather than being completed by inference.
sections.third: A published portfolio keeps working without the AI provider or PDF parser.
sections.secondTitle: What if a fact is missing?
sections.fourthTitle: Can I have more than one portfolio?
sections.fourth: Yes — one account can hold several portfolios, each with its own address and its own review before publishing.
sections.fifthTitle: Can I take a page down?
sections.fifth: Unpublishing or deleting a portfolio is available from the dashboard at any time; nothing requires contacting support.
sections.sixth: The account settings page shows the current plan and what it includes; a trial period applies to new subscriptions.

accessibility.title: Accessibility is part of the publishing contract
accessibility.description: The editor and every public portfolio target WCAG 2.2 AA across keyboard, touch, contrast, and structure.

sections.first: Landmarks, headings, labels, and current-page states support navigation.
sections.second: Visible focus and touch-sized controls serve keyboard and mobile readers.
sections.third: Gallery images require useful alternatives and motion respects reduced-motion settings.
sections.fourth: Every public page and the editor itself are tested against WCAG 2.2 AA rather than relying on the framework's defaults.
sections.fifth: Reordering sections, uploading files, and reviewing extracted fields all work from the keyboard, not only the published result.
sections.sixth: The contact page has a dedicated path for accessibility reports, including what assistive technology surfaced the issue.

terms.title: Terms written around control and responsible use
terms.description: Use the service for content you are entitled to publish and review every fact before making it public.

sections.first: You retain responsibility for the professional information you publish.
sections.second: Do not upload malware, impersonate another person, or evade access controls.
sections.third: You can unpublish or delete your data using the controls provided.
sections.firstTitle: You're responsible for what you publish
sections.fourth: Only the reviewed snapshot and the assets you explicitly attach are stored for a published portfolio — see the privacy page for the full boundary.
sections.fifth: Material changes are reflected here and, where relevant, called out on the changelog page.
sections.sixth: The contact page reaches the team for anything these terms don't make clear.

changelog.title: What changed, and why it matters
changelog.description: A concise record of product changes that affect authoring, privacy, accessibility, or public output.

sections.first: Document changes explain new fields and migration behavior.
sections.second: Security changes identify strengthened boundaries without exposing exploit details.
sections.third: Renderer changes call out visible behavior and accessibility improvements.
sections.fourth: A portfolio is a durable address — knowing what changed under it matters as much as knowing what's new.
sections.fifth: A change that affects what a visitor sees or what an owner can control gets an entry, not just a version bump.
sections.sixth: The contact page is the way to flag a change that should have been documented here and wasn't.
